outlook: Soybeans gained again Tuesday, with January futures up 5¼ cents to $12.34 after President Trump said a trade deal including large US soybean purchases may be done; details could come in the coming days. Wheat fell across all three classes on a stronger US dollar: Chicago December lost 7¼ cents to $5.69¾ and Minneapolis December spring wheat slipped 3¼ cents to $6.36¾, even as Russia's November grain shipments are running far below last year. December corn ended nearly unchanged at $4.34, pulled lower by wheat, with the US corn harvest now 94% complete. ICE January canola eased C$2.60 to C$773.20, and Minneapolis terminal corn and soybean bids widened on the low end.
